This integration shows in Gladys the garage doors and gates driven by an
**ismartgate** (PRO, LITE, Mini) or **GogoGate2** gateway, and adds buttons to
open and close them, through the local API of the gateway, on your network,
without its cloud.

**Never tested with a real device**: the integration follows the ismartgate
library (the one of the Home Assistant "Gogogate2 and ismartgate"
integration), but nobody has tried it on a real gateway yet. This local API is
not documented by the maker. Your feedback is welcome.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with ismartgate.

## In Gladys

One device per door set up on the gateway (a door that has a name in its
app):

| Feature           | Detail                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Garage door, Gate | opening sensor, read only (open / closed)                 |
| Open, Close       | buttons (only for an output in garage door or pulse mode) |
| Temperature       | wireless sensor only                                      |
| Sensor battery    | in %, wireless sensor only                                |

## Installation

1. Give the gateway a fixed IP address in your router.
2. In the ismartgate app, preferably create a user for Gladys, with only the
   doors it may command.
3. In Gladys, install the ismartgate integration from the store, pick the
   family (ismartgate or GogoGate2), type the IP address, the user name and
   the password.
4. Add the doors from the Discovery tab.

The password is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only
to your gateway. The local API carries it scrambled (AES) in the address of
the request, over HTTP: on an ismartgate the key comes from the user name and
the password, but on a **GogoGate2 the key is the same for every gateway and
public**: anyone who captures the traffic of your local network can read the
user name and the password. Use a dedicated user, with a password you use
nowhere else.

## Command safety

The gateway only knows one command: **a pulse** on the relay of the door, the
same to open and to close, like the button of a remote control. A pulse while
the door moves may stop it or send it back. So:

- a door is never a switch: a "turn everything off" of a voice assistant or a
  scene cannot reach it;
- **opening and closing are off by default**: closing and opening are the
  same pulse (on a moving door, "Close" may reopen it), hence one option;
  without it, Gladys neither opens nor closes. Turn on "Allow opening and
  closing" so that the dashboard, the scenes and the voice assistants can
  open and close. The permission is checked when the command arrives, after
  the fresh read and right before sending;
- every command reads the gateway just before acting: the gateway must be the
  same one (its id), the door set up, in garage door or pulse mode, with a
  known state. "Open" only pulses a door read closed, "Close" only a door read
  open; in the wanted state, nothing is sent; with no state (sensor missing
  or faulty), nothing is sent;
- an (allowed) close never waits behind the openings, and gets one try even
  during a pause asked by the gateway or after refused credentials; a close,
  even refused, cancels at once an opening of the same door not sent yet;
- one pulse at a time per door, and after each pulse no other one on that
  door until it is read in the other state, or until the "travel time" (30 s
  by default) plus 5 s has passed;
- a command that cannot leave within 3.5 seconds is refused unsent; a pulse
  sent without an answer is reported "sent, without confirmation", then the
  door is read again.

**Limit** (option on): the gateway does not say whether a door is closing
(the sensor stays "open" until the end of the travel). If someone has just
started closing with a remote and a close leaves Gladys at the same moment,
the pulse may stop the door or send it back towards opening, as a second
press on the remote would. Gladys never does it twice in a row itself (the
guard above, kept across a restart too). A door without a sensor gives no
state: Gladys sends it no pulse.

There is no "Stop" button: the gateway has no stop command.

## Failures

- Credentials refused: the gateway is no longer asked, then again after
  15 min, 1 h, 6 h and every 24 h, even after a restart; saving other
  credentials tries again at once, "Test the connection" once the refresh
  interval has passed.
- A gateway that asks to wait (HTTP 429 or 5xx) is paused for one minute to
  six hours, even after a restart: no read, no opening; an allowed close
  still gets one try.
- A door removed from the gateway (no name) is shown unreachable and named
  in the status.
- A gateway that does not answer is read again after 30 s, 1, 2 then 5 min,
  never faster than the refresh interval. "Test the connection", a
  reconnection of Gladys or a restart never read faster than the interval.
- If another gateway answers at the address (DHCP lease), its doors show up
  in the Discovery tab and the old ones are shown unreachable.

## Limits

- No automatic search on the network: type the IP address.
- No camera, no outputs in on/off mode (shown read only), no access through
  the ismartgate cloud.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que ismartgate te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your ismartgate or GogoGate2 gateway, on your local network | `section` | No | Reads the doors of the gateway (open or closed, temperature and battery of the wireless sensors) through its local API, without its cloud, and adds "Open" and "Close" buttons. Give the gateway a fixed IP address in your router, type it below with the user name and password of its app, then add the doors from the Discovery tab. Never tested with a real device. Unofficial integration, not affiliated with ismartgate. |
| Gateway | `select` | No | The family of your gateway: ismartgate (PRO, LITE, Mini) or the older GogoGate2. |
| IP address of the gateway | `string` | No | For example 192.168.1.30 (add :port if it is not 80). |
| User name | `string` | No | A user of the gateway (its app or web page). A user of its own for Gladys is best, with only the doors it may use. |
| Password | `secret` | No | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to your gateway, scrambled the way its local API asks (with the fixed key of every GogoGate2, so readable by anyone who captures your local network traffic). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the gateway is read, in seconds. |
| Opening and closing | `section` | No | The gateway only knows one command: a pulse on the relay of the door, the same for opening and closing. So each door is shown with buttons, never as a switch, and Gladys sends a pulse only from the other end: "Open" from a door read closed just now, "Close" from a door read open, nothing when the sensor gives no state. As a pulse on a moving door may stop it or send it back open, opening AND closing are refused until you allow them below. A close always cancels an opening still waiting to leave. After a pulse, no other one on that door until it is seen moving, or until the travel time has passed: a second pulse would stop it or send it back. |
| Allow opening and closing | `boolean` | No | Off by default: Gladys then neither opens nor closes (closing is the same pulse). On: the dashboard, the scenes and the voice assistants can open and close the doors and gates. |
| Travel time (s) | `number` | No | How long your slowest door or gate takes to open or close, in seconds. After a pulse, no other pulse on that door for this time plus 5 s, unless it is seen moving. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the features added from now on, and for the command errors. |

## Cómo instalar ismartgate en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: ismartgate aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-ismartgate:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ismartgate](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ismartgate).

ismartgate requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

ismartgate es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
